Both checks green on the committed state. Here's where things stand.

## Summary

The work for all 3 related "AI Architecture / Software-First AI-Second Philosophy" findings is **complete and committed locally** on branch `gap-ai-arch-software-first` (3 commits). I read the real code first, and the findings' numbers were stale — I corrected that rather than blindly acting on the stale text.

**What I found vs. the findings:**
- **Findings 1 & 3** (software-first not applied to every AI call site): the gate is real — `classifyExecutionWithReliability()` in `software-coverage-service.ts`, wired into the capability/task-execution/chat paths. But ~15 direct `callLLM*` sites (vision OCR, digitization, prompt-eval, ai-team dispatch) bypass it, most legitimately AI-only. The real gap was a **discipline gap**: nothing required a justification when a new LLM call site was added. I closed it with a CI check (`scripts/check-ai-call-site-justification.mjs`) requiring each `callLLM*` site to carry either a software-first gate OR an inline `// software-first: AI-only because <reason>` comment — *not* a blanket "must call classifyExecution" (that'd be wrong for OCR). Added honest inline justifications to the 7 legitimately-AI-only sites; the 8 gated sites pass via file-level gate.
- **Finding 2** ("25 of 247 VCEL engines"): **stale** — real state is 211 of 247 implemented, 26 wired into Chain Selector dispatch. I didn't re-implement engines (multi-day work each, out of scope). Instead I closed the recommendation's real sub-gap: `tokenUsageLedger` doesn't track per-domain AI-call volume, so "prioritize next engines by AI-call-volume-per-domain" wasn't computable. Added `getDomainAiCallVolume()` + a veridian_admin-gated route, with the honest limitation documented.

Wired the check into `ci.yml` and self-anchored it in `check-guardrail-presence.mjs` (Rule 9). No schema/migration; didn't touch `permission-service.ts` (in-flight RBAC worker), `auth-guard.ts`, or any engine.

**Verification:** `check-guardrail-presence.mjs` (90 markers) and the new check (15 sites) both pass locally. `tsc --noEmit` shows zero logic errors in changed files (only environmental `Cannot find module` noise — this sandbox has no `node_modules`/`bun`; CI installs deps). I negative-tested the new check (correctly flags an ungated call; passes gated + justified).

## One blocker — needs your call

I couldn't push the branch. This session's `gh` token has scopes `gist, read:org, repo` but **not `workflow`**, so GitHub refuses any push containing the `.github/workflows/ci.yml` change. I isolated and proved this: pushing with the `ci.yml` change excluded succeeds; with it included, rejected. Every other file pushes fine.

**Option A (preferred):** grant `workflow` scope to the token (or push branch `gap-ai-arch-software-first` yourself), then I open the single coherent PR — CI wiring in the same PR as the check it enforces.

**Option B (fallback):** I split it now — push everything except `ci.yml`, open that PR, and the one-line `ai-call-site-justification` CI job goes in a tiny follow-up PR you push.

Which would you like? (I haven't pushed anything except a temporary isolation branch, which I already deleted from the remote.)
